title: Richard Bellman and the Naming of "Dynamic Programming" (1950s)
explainer: Richard Bellman developed the mathematics of multistage decision processes at the RAND Corporation in the early-to-mid 1950s. By his own account in his autobiography, he chose the deliberately bland name "dynamic programming" partly to avoid drawing suspicion from a Secretary of Defense hostile to mathematical research, since RAND depended on Air Force funding. The word "programming" there originally meant planning or scheduling, not computer programming, which is why the name can feel disconnected from what the technique actually does.
